title: Social media
subtitle: post, share, follow, tag, privacy settings
summary: Use the everyday language of social media - posting, sharing, following and tagging - and talk about profiles, notifications and privacy settings.

lesson.heading: Social media verbs
lesson.text: Most social media activity is described with a small set of verbs: you **post** something, other people **share**, **like** or **comment on** it, and you **follow** or **subscribe to** the people whose posts you want to see.

examples.text: My friend **posted** a video of her baby and it was **shared** over a thousand times.
Send me a **friend request**, and then you can see the pictures I took.
I probably **update my status** about twice a week. I like telling people what I'm doing.
Over 100,000 people **subscribe to** his video channel and **follow** him on Twitter.

lesson.heading: Noun and verb - the same word
rows: I wrote a **comment** on her status.

lesson.heading: Using a social media app
lesson.text: When you join an **app**, you create a **profile**, **upload** a photo and include some basic information. You can then **post updates**, **share links** to things you find interesting, or **comment on** other people's profiles.

examples.text: You can **rate** videos from one to five stars.
You can see how many **views** or **likes** your post got.
examples.note: views = the number of times people have watched it; likes = the number of times people have clicked 'like'

examples.text: It's annoying that you can't turn off **notifications** when a friend writes something new.
examples.note: notifications = messages that tell you when something has happened

lesson.heading: Profiles and timelines
lesson.text: Your **profile** is the page with information about you, and your **profile picture** is the photo of you at the top of it. Your **timeline** is the collection of photos and other posts on your profile.

examples.text: Often your **profile picture** is **public**, but you can usually make posts on your **timeline** **private**.
To enter the competition, share this picture on your **timeline** before 8 pm on Friday.

lesson.heading: Online privacy
lesson.text: It is worth thinking about who can see your personal information. Check your **privacy settings** regularly and make sure you understand who can see what you post.

examples.text: If you have to give personal information when you create an **account**, make sure it is kept **private**.
The **default** setting for new posts is Friends Only.
examples.note: the default = what happens automatically if you don't change it

lesson.heading: Tags and direct messages
lesson.text: If you are **tagged** in someone else's post, your name and a link to your profile are added to it - and a lot of people you don't know may see it. For anything private, use a **direct message**, which only the people in the conversation can see.

examples.text: Please don't **tag** me in any of those photos - I look terrible.
You can ask people to remove the **tag** if necessary.
If you want to buy the skirt, please send me a **direct message**.
**Delete** old accounts on sites you are not using any more - you might forget what information they contain.

lesson.text: Notice the difference between public (everyone can see it) and private (only the people you choose can see it) - your privacy settings decide which is which.

exercises.prompt: If you liked this video, please ___ it with your friends.
exercises.explanation: You share a post or a video with other people.

exercises.prompt: I hate it when people ___ hundreds of photos from their holiday.
exercises.explanation: To post something is to put it on social media.

exercises.prompt: Do you know Monica Coto? She's just sent me a friend ___ on Facebook.
exercises.explanation: A friend request asks someone to connect with you.

exercises.prompt: I just updated my ___ to tell people we've arrived safely at the hotel.
exercises.explanation: You update your status to say what you are doing.

exercises.prompt: You can ___ to our channel, and we'll email you when a new video comes out.
exercises.explanation: You subscribe to a channel; you follow a person.

exercises.prompt: Mo likes to ___ chefs and food writers on Twitter.
exercises.explanation: You follow someone to see everything they post.

exercises.prompt: I've just uploaded ___ of Saturday's football match to the team Facebook page.
exercises.explanation: You upload photos and videos; you write comments.

exercises.prompt: Yi Ling ___ a lot of updates about her training for the 10k run.
exercises.explanation: You post an update; other people then view it.

exercises.prompt: Jo posted a really interesting article about Formula 1 racing, but it didn't get any ___.
exercises.explanation: Likes are countable; rate is a verb, not a noun here.

exercises.prompt: Did you ___ that restaurant we went to? I'd give it one star.
exercises.explanation: You rate something from one to five stars.

exercises.prompt: Elena made a video for the animal charity she works for and it got 3,000 ___.
exercises.explanation: Views are the number of times people have watched it.

exercises.prompt: An old friend ___ on one of my photos, asking where I was living now.
exercises.explanation: You comment on a photo or a status.

exercises.prompt: What do we call each of these?

pairs.left: the page with information about the user
the page where a person's photos and posts appear
the message you get when something new happens

exercises.prompt: I'm a teacher, so I make sure everything in my profile is ___. I don't want my students to see it.
exercises.explanation: Private means only the people you choose can see it.

exercises.prompt: To find your ___ settings, click on the 'lock' icon at the top of the screen.
exercises.explanation: Privacy settings are the choices about what people see on your profile.

exercises.prompt: To create an ___, you have to give your email address and a password.
exercises.explanation: You create an account when you join a site.

exercises.prompt: The ___ setting for new posts on this site is Friends Only, but it's easy to change.
exercises.explanation: The default is what happens automatically if you don't change it.

exercises.prompt: Sort the words into things you do and things you get.
